summary.title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 2)
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a basic feed-forward neural network in Rust, with idiomatic iterator-based propagation, seeded random initialization, and approximate float testing.
keywords: rust iterator fold map zip sum
how to test random functions rust
takeaways: Model a feed-forward network as Network, Layer and Neuron structs, with propagate() passing values through each layer
Replace manual loops with idiomatic iterator combinators such as fold, map, collect, zip and sum
Make randomness testable by injecting a seeded RNG (rand_chacha) instead of calling thread_rng inside the code
Compare floats approximately (approx crate or an epsilon margin) rather than exactly, because f32 cannot represent many decimals
summary.summary: The second part of the Learning to Fly series sets up a Rust workspace and builds a basic feed-forward neural network from scratch. It walks through designing Network, Layer and Neuron types, implementing propagate() with iterator idioms, and deciding when to use assert versus Result for input-size checks. It then covers constructors that generate random weights with the rand crate and explains how to make that randomness testable by passing in a seeded RNG. The post ends with floating-point pitfalls and tests using the approx crate.
